newsitem.title: USA: Federal agency probing alleged arson in Boston.
newsitem.headline: Federal agency probing alleged arson in Boston.

text.p: Federal arson investigators have joined Boston police and fire officials in working on a case of alleged, and possibly racially motivated, arson.

Police spokeswoman Dilani Yoganratnam said there were no named suspects and she could not confirm racial motivation in the burning of an unoccupied house in the 96.8 percent white West Roxbury section that a black family was buying.
But on Sunday Police Commissioner Paul Evans said: "We're not blind. We can't ignore (the sale). The original officers saw the possibility of this being a racial crime."
William Picket, a spokesman for the federal Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms Bureau, would confirm only that his agency was taking part in the probe.

The daughter of the current white homeowners told police she was awakened by a noise she thought was made by a prowler and discovered the blaze in a rear sun porch at 3:30 a.m. Sunday. No one was hurt in the fire, which fire officials said caused $100,000 in damage to the home.

Although the West Roxbury area is inhabited mostly by middle class whites, many of them civil servants, neighbours and area politicians were quick to defend the area as not having sharp racial divisions.

Boston has seen considerable racial strife over the past quarter-century, including sometimes-violent school desegregation and charges of real estate agency and bank redlining of home sales and mortgage loans.

"Those are serious accusations to make," Mayor Thomas Menino told the Boston Globe, speaking of the suspected racial motivation in the West Roxbury case. "We won't tolerate such horrendous acts," he said. "We're going to prosecute as far as we can."
